records.sourceAnchor: Original guideline sections 4.1-4.2 for individual micro enterprises; official MoFPI individual-unit page; 18 May 2022 modification; portal notices and component summaries
observations: PMFME is a centrally sponsored package with distinct component routes. It must not be represented as one universal subsidy: individual micro units, FPOs/FPCs, SHGs and cooperatives, common infrastructure, SHG seed capital, branding/marketing and capacity building have different beneficiaries, application paths and benefit structures.

For the individual-unit route, the official MoFPI page describes a credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost, capped at ₹10 lakh per unit, with minimum 10% beneficiary contribution and the balance financed through a bank loan. Training support is linked to supported capital-investment units and to other existing district units processing ODOP products.

The 18 May 2022 official modification says both existing and new micro food processing enterprises may be considered for expansion/upgradation or setting up a new unit; ODOP products receive preference, but other micro enterprises may also be considered. The modification also points to an Annexure-I list of food-processing activities that are not eligible, so unknown activity classification must not be treated as eligible.

The official portal separately describes common-infrastructure support, SHG seed capital, 50% branding/marketing support for eligible groups or an SPV, ODOP alignment and capacity building. These values and beneficiary groups must remain separate from the individual ₹10 lakh credit-linked subsidy and must not be added into one total eligible value.

Official status material is time-sensitive. Earlier scheme material described a five-year period beginning 2020-21, while an official February 2025 parliamentary answer states operation up to FY 2025-26. The portal currently shows a maintenance notice and a 30 December 2025 clarification, but the reviewed sources do not yet establish a post-FY2025-26 extension or a currently open national application window.

Application access is mediated through the PMFME portal and, for group routes, State/District Nodal Agencies. A user-facing record must show the state/district route, bank-credit dependency, ODOP preference, required project and identity evidence, and the difference between recommendation/sanction/disbursement; it must not promise approval or treat portal statistics as an applicant entitlement.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm the canonical current guideline and all later modifications, including the 30 December 2025 primary-processing clarification, and determine whether any official extension beyond FY2025-26 exists.

Verify whether individual applications are currently accepted, paused or closed while the portal is under maintenance; record any state-specific windows and do not infer a national deadline from historical portal pages.

Extract and version Annexure-I excluded activities, ODOP lists, state/district nodal contacts, bank route, application forms, document checklists and the exact project-cost rules for individual applicants.
Keep individual, group, common-infrastructure, SHG seed-capital, branding/marketing and training records separate, with distinct eligibility rules, benefits, documents and application steps.

Validate existing/new-unit treatment, legal-form eligibility, beneficiary contribution, bank-loan conditions, technical civil-work limits, subsidy release/recovery conditions and any state-level implementation variations.
Classify the opportunity as active, paused, closed or historical only after the post-FY2025-26 status and live portal route are confirmed by a reviewer.

publicationGuard.reason: PMFME has multiple component routes and conflicting/aging period evidence. The post-FY2025-26 status, current portal availability, 2025 clarification, excluded activities, state route and component-specific fine print require human review before publication.
